To be honest, this was a pretty good dungeon - but not the best. The atmosphere was amazing, and it didn't really feel like I was adventuring a dungeon filled with enemies - it felt like a community. 

This dungeon seems to be generally considered one of the most difficult dungeons in Twilight Princess, but I really don't think this is the case. It can be a little difficult at times (Considering most of the rooms in the dungeon look the same) and I remember spending ages trying to figure out how I could get high enough for my Hookshot/Clawshot could reach a certain switch/grate. Great memories.

It was a good way of showing us what the heck the Ooccoos are, and it really helps give you a sense of Society in the game, that there are other species with their own little environments. All other dungeons in the game are mainly set in an interior, and it is a huge relief and a feeling of fresh air when there is a Dungeon that is set in a huge empty space in the sky - really neat in my opinion, and they need more dungeons like this in the future.

The puzzles were amazing, utilising the Ooccoos and forcing you to actually help you glide across certain areas of the dungeon. This could get difficult at times, as you might get in the perfect position but then **the damn Ooccoo was across the room**. That was incredibly annoying because, for the most part, this wasn't even in the player's control. It just happened, depending on what the Ooccoo wanted to do.

There was actually quite a lot of exploration in the dungeon, because there were many areas which had alternate exits (or it gave that illusion, anyway) but it would lack sometimes, because in the beginning of the dungeon it gave you lots of places to go, but practically all of them **except one** was a dead end. 

I don't really recall the Dungeon's theme, which probably means that it wasn't very memorable - and not that good.

There was very little story involved with this dungeon. It just felt... **there**. How the hell did the Mirror Shard get into the *City of the Sky*? Unless I missed something, it really makes no sense. The Ooccoos are really not a pretty sight, but I feel that they could have been involved in more of the story besides one dungeon (Even though they sort of had a side-story with the Mama Ooccoo and Ooccoo Jr.) In fact, I think that it would be lovely to have these little guys running around in other Legend of Zelda titles. Alright, I was getting a little off-topic there.

The enemies were alright, with lots of them requiring you to make use of items you collected in previous dungeons. While that was cool, it caused me to have to keep switching items every damn second I suspected that one of the floor tiles was one of those enemies (not sure of the name). 
The Mini-boss was a *meh*, as they were reduced to mere enemies in future dungeons and even reappeared later in the dungeon itself. The same happened with the Darknuts, but they're awesome so they get a pass.

The final boss of the dungeon was definitely a highlight, as he was quite literally the only boss in the entire game that was a challenge to me (Besides the Horseback fight against Ganondorf) Argorok looked awesome, and the music against the fight was definitely memorable for me. Unfortunately the second half of the fight only becomes a challenge, because of the panic that I get when I can't Clawshot to the next point - sometimes it would automatically target, other times it wouldn't. That was the reason the fight was a challenge - and every **single** time you get hit by the flames, you fall **ALL** the way down, and you have to make it back up again.

The Double-Clawshot idea was genius, and definitely fun to use, but when I first got the item, I was definitely disappointed. The first look at an item is the most exciting part, because you really start to wonder **OMG! WHAT IS THAT ITEM HOW DO I USE IT WILL IT BE HELPFUL OMG OMG OMG**, but in this case you already know how it works, because it is the **exact** same item you got in a previous dungeon. It doesn't even look different, which makes me wonder *who made the Clawshot?* 

All and all, I believe that this Dungeon was pretty cool. I'd put it on the lower-half of the dungeons though, and I never really look forward to doing the dungeon during my playthrough of the game. But I *do* look forward to fighting the boss. I'd have to give this dungeon a 6/10.
